title: Stalkwise flatness over the affine direct-image algebra
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-pc-scheme], and let $g:(X,O_X)\to(Y,f_*O_X)$ be the canonical ringed-space morphism [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. For every $x\in X$, the canonical stalk ring homomorphism $(f_*O_X)_{f(x)}\to O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence, affine stalk calculation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AVW

proof.text: Choose an affine neighborhood Spec B of f(x); its inverse image is Spec A. For p = x and q = f(x), distinguished opens D(b) with b outside q are cofinal neighborhoods. Their inverse images have section rings A localized at the image of b. Taking the stalk colimit gives S^{-1}A for S the image of B minus q. Germ compatibility identifies the source-to-target map with S^{-1}A → A_p.
S avoids p, so A_p is a further localization of S^{-1}A. Localization is flat. The calculation applies at each point; the empty source case is vacuous.
